core_api.py::_accept_loop.ends: open connections are capped at max_connections and a connection leaves the set when it closes; refusal workers are capped at MAX_REFUSAL_THREADS and each ends when its refusal is answered, a burst past either gets a refusal row and a closed socket, so neither count accumulates

core_api.py::_ask.ends: a per-call byte cap on a question; a longer one is refused too_large, nothing is kept

core_api.py::_clean.ends: a recursion depth bound on one reply being filtered; deeper values become None, it ends with the call, nothing accumulates

core_api.py::_confirmed.ends: pending confirmations are capped per token; each expires after CONFIRM_SECONDS and expired ones are purged when a new one is asked for, or goes when it is used

core_api.py::_label.ends: a per-call byte cut of one source label as it is written into a delivered line; it ends with the call, nothing accumulates

core_api.py::_message_params.ends: a per-call byte cap on one message; a longer one is refused too_large, nothing is kept

core_api.py::_need_str.ends: a per-call length and control-character check on a caller-supplied id or short string; it ends with the call, nothing accumulates

core_api.py::_need_text.ends: a per-call byte cap on free text (a note, question or reply); a longer one is refused too_large, nothing is kept

core_api.py::_push_params.ends: a per-call byte cap on one pushed note; a longer one is refused too_large and no intent row is written

core_api.py::_read_json.ends: a per-read byte cap on one records file; a larger file reads as None (unknown), nothing is kept

core_api.py::_read_jsonl_file.ends: a per-read byte cap on one records file; a larger file reads only its newest tail and the reply says incomplete, nothing is kept

core_api.py::_rewrite_tokens.ends: a byte cap on the token store (tokens.json); a larger store is refused on read and a write that would exceed it is refused before replacing, so the file stops at the cap; revoking a token removes its row (an unknown token is refused exactly like a revoked one) and the next mint also drops any row still marked revoked, so revoked tokens never use up the store

core_api.py::_subscribe.ends: live subscriptions are capped overall and per token; a subscription leaves the list when its reader closes, is dropped as too slow, or reaches its limit

core_api.py::_take_push_allowance.ends: a per-token rate limit of PUSH_PER_WINDOW notes per window; times older than the window are dropped on each call; on each call every other token's list is also removed when its window is empty or its token is revoked or unknown, so only tokens with a note in the last window keep a list

core_api.py::_tokens_used.ends: a per-call range check on a reported token count; an out-of-range value is refused, nothing is kept

core_api.py::changes_diff.ends: a per-call byte cut of one diff in the reply (truncated says so); the diffs record itself is bounded by its own retention

core_api.py::handle.ends: a per-reply cut of any list longer than LIST_MAX; the reply says incomplete, nothing is kept

core_api.py::offer.ends: a per-subscriber buffer of undelivered events; when it is full the subscriber is marked dropped and closed, which frees its slot and its buffer

core_api.py::readline.ends: a per-line byte cap on one request line; a longer line is refused too_large and the connection closed, the read buffer never exceeds the limit

learning_store.py::wake_reconcile_page.ends: RS-E E2a-9 (review round 1): at most 64 project rows examined per locked read; the pass continues from its cursor page by page, so every project is reached however many there are

project_wake.py::send_wake.ends: RS-E E2a-7: one reply frame of at most 16 KiB per publication; a reply past it ends that exchange (WakeUnavailable, the write keeps its unpublished flag and retries)

learning_store.py::<module>.ends: RS-E E2c-2: START_CLAIM_SQL / START_CLAIM_AFTER_SQL read at most one claim batch (64) of due rows per locked step; a full batch is followed by the next one at once (review round 1, HIGH 1), from the starter's cursor, and a claimed row leaves the set until its attempt ends

learning_store.py::outstanding_starts.ends: RS-E E2c-10: one page of at most 64 outstanding claims per read; the stranded pass reads page after page from its cursor, and a claim leaves the set once released or ended

project_start.py::_reconcile_stranded.ends: RS-E E2c-10: a page shorter than START_CLAIM_BATCH ends the pass; a full page continues after its last claim, so every outstanding claim is reached

learning_store.py::probation_starts.ends: RS-E E2c-4 (review round 1, HIGH 4): one page of at most 64 kept probations per read; the starter's pass reads page after page from its cursor, and a probation leaves the set once its host served it out or ended

project_start.py::_reconcile_probations.ends: RS-E E2c-4 (review round 1, HIGH 4): a page shorter than START_CLAIM_BATCH ends the pass; a full page continues after its last row, so every kept probation is reached

project_start.py::_claim.ends: RS-E E2c-2 (review round 1, LOW): START_QUEUE_LIMIT (1,024) claims wait in memory at once; a worker taking one frees its place, a full queue is looked at again every tick, and a stopping collector releases what is left

project_start.py::_worker.ends: RS-E E2c-2 (review round 1, LOW, HIGH 3): START_SLOTS (2) starts at once, a dead collector's surviving child holding one; a slot is free again when its start ends (its outcome kept, or retried by the starter thread) or the surviving child serves, ends or reaches twice the start timeout

project_start.py::_record_child.ends: RS-E E2c-10 (review round 1, HIGH 2): SETTLE_TRIES tries to keep a child's pid on its claim, per start; past them the child is still timed, killed at twice the timeout and reaped by its worker

hold_migration.py::__init__.ends: Temporary migration batching only; a batch of at most 64 source rows advances the durable cursor and ends at commit; progress is removed on validated publication.

hold_migration.py::batches.ends: Temporary migration batching only; a batch of at most 64 source rows advances the durable cursor and ends at commit; progress is removed on validated publication.

memory_holds.py::drop.ends: Reuses MAX_RETIRED_RUNS: the oldest memory tombstone is removed on insertion past the bound; durable project hold tombstones retain replay protection independently.

project_driver.py::_request.ends: the held run.register intake (RS-B-4 final fix) is bounded by MAX_INTAKE, the same bound as the driver's connection intake: held registers leave when the start-up memory recovery is done or failed, or at WAIT_SECONDS, and a register past the bound gets the plain bounded refusal (history_service_unavailable) at once

ledger_owner_queue.py::__post_init__.ends: construction-time validation of the queue's own limits (requests, projects, per-project, their product, the wait bound); nothing is counted, an out-of-range limit is refused at construction

ledger_owner_queue.py::offer.ends: queued and running requests count until whole completion and acknowledgement, then leave; a full queue or project refuses the new offer as named, counted overflow (busy)

ledger_owner_queue.py::_count.ends: refusal counts keep at most MAX_REFUSAL_CALLERS caller buckets; further callers fold into 'other' with totals kept, so the map never grows

learning_store.py::publish_health.ends: Published health is a working set of eight snapshots. The oldest publication is evicted when a new project enters; durable registrations and admission are never capped.

learning_store.py::_health_refresh_for.ends: Outstanding health refreshes: one per project root, at most MAX_PUBLISHED_PROJECT_HEALTH; each entry is pruned once its refresh is handled, which the owner always acknowledges (refused or run). Past the bound a cold read answers the existing ledger_busy.
